The "betting_calibration" primitive formalizes the process of adjusting model outputs so that predicted probabilities match observed frequencies. Mathematically, this is achieved through maximum likelihood estimation or kernel density fitting against historical settlement data. The \mathcal{C}(\cdot) operator ensures that our predictions are not only accurate but also well-spread across the probability spectrum, preventing overfitting to recent price movements. In practice, we monitor the telemetry metrics such as calibration loss to detect regime shifts (e.g., sudden liquidity changes) that may require recalibration. It was later formalized in machine learning as a calibration curve by Platt (1999) and extended to high-dimensional settings using isotonic regression. Our use here generalizes these ideas to handle streaming, heterogeneous sports betting data.
